source: FWC recreational saltwater regulations (myfwc.com) — Florida Atlantic, Northeast zone, Volusia County

amberjack.note: Atlantic season is Jan-Mar and May-Dec; closed all April. Lesser Amberjack and Banded Rudderfish 14" to 22" fork, 5 per person aggregate. Almaco is unregulated.

bonito.note: Unregulated species: the default bag is two fish or 100 lb per person per day, whichever is more.

flounder.note: Closed Oct 15 - Nov 30 statewide, in state and federal water.

grouper.size: 24" min Gag & Black, 20" min Red & Scamp
grouper.note: Atlantic season opens May 1 — Gag through Aug 1, the rest through Dec 31. Nassau and Goliath are prohibited. Gag vessel limit 2.

hogfish.note: Atlantic season May 1 - Oct 31, state and federal water alike.

jack.note: Jack Crevalle is unregulated — two fish or 100 lb per person, whichever is more. Almaco and Banded Rudderfish carry their own limits.

mackerel.size: 12" fork min Spanish, 24" fork min King
mackerel.note: King bag is 2 on the Atlantic coast; the Gulf allows 3. Cero is unregulated.

mahi.note: On a for-hire trip the vessel limit is the bag times the number of paying customers; captain and crew may not keep a bag.

permit.note: No more than 2 fish over 22" per vessel.

redfish.note: Northeast zone. South of the NSB South Causeway — the Indian River Lagoon zone, which takes in Mosquito Lagoon — Redfish are catch and release only.

shark.note: No minimum on Blacktip, Bonnethead, Atlantic Sharpnose and the rest of Group 1; 54" fork on Bull, Nurse, Spinner and the rest of Group 2. Many species are prohibited outright, and fishing from shore needs a free permit and course.

sheepshead.note: Vessel limit 50 per trip during March and April. State limits extend into federal water.

snapper.size: 10" min Mangrove, 18" min Mutton, 8" min Lane
snapper.note: Atlantic Red Snapper 20", 2 per person — open in state water, closed in federal. Mangrove is 12" and 10 per person once you are beyond 3 mi.

snook.note: Snook permit required. Closed Dec 15 - Jan 31 and Jun 1 - Aug 31 in the Northeast and Indian River Lagoon zones alike.

tarpon.note: A Tarpon over 40" must stay in the water. Harvest only with a state tarpon tag, one per person per year.

triggerfish.note: Atlantic Gray Triggerfish are open year-round, inside the 20-fish snapper-grouper aggregate. Queen Triggerfish are a marine life species and must be landed alive.

trout.note: Northeast zone. South of the NSB South Causeway — the Indian River Lagoon zone — the bag is 2 and the season closes Nov 1 - Dec 31.

whiting.note: Gulf Kingfish (whiting) is unregulated — two fish or 100 lb per person, whichever is more.

lines: First published. Every limit read off FWC's own species pages that day.

Ten values were corrected against what the app had carried since Build 279 — Triggerfish (bag 1 to 10, and no January–April closure on the Atlantic), Seatrout (3 fish, none over 19"), Redfish (4 per vessel), Amberjack (April only), King Mackerel (2), Sheepshead (50 per vessel in March and April), Permit (2 over 22" per vessel), Black Drum (one fish over 24" allowed), Atlantic Red Snapper (open in state water), and the 2-fish/100-lb default bag on Bonito, Jack Crevalle and Whiting.
